title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Teens With Tighter Safety Guardrails and Parental Controls
excerpt: The $852 billion AI company rolls out a dedicated teen experience with quiet hours, study mode, and age-detection technology as it faces multiple lawsuits alleging its chatbot harmed young people.
body:
• OpenAI has launched "ChatGPT for Teens," a dedicated experience with stronger safety protections for users aged 13 to 17, including age-detection AI that applies safeguards regardless of the birthdate in a user's profile.
  • New features include 90-minute usage nudges, customizable "Quiet Hours" and "Study Hours," protections against the chatbot expressing personal feelings toward users, and alerts for parents related to eating disorders.
  • The launch comes as OpenAI faces multiple lawsuits from families alleging ChatGPT contributed to the harm or deaths of their children, including a recent Massachusetts murder case.
  • Nearly a third of American teens use AI chatbots daily, with ChatGPT being the most popular, according to a December 2025 Pew Research Center study.

OpenAI has rolled out a new "ChatGPT for Teens" experience designed to provide additional safety protections for its youngest users, the company announced on Tuesday. The move arrives amid mounting legal pressure and public scrutiny over the risks AI chatbots pose to minors.

What the New Experience Includes

The dedicated teen version brings together a suite of tools and safety protections that OpenAI has developed over the past year into a single, cohesive experience. Users who identify at sign-up as being under 18 will be automatically placed into the protective settings.

https://x.com/NeuroPulseahqr/status/2089748030194954659

Key features include nudges for teen users to take a break after 90 minutes of activity within a three-hour window. Parents can set "Quiet Hours" when ChatGPT is entirely unavailable, and "Study Hours" that default to the platform's guided learning mode.

OpenAI has also improved protections to prevent ChatGPT from expressing personal feelings toward a user and added reminders cautioning teens to think twice before uploading private or sensitive images to the chatbot.

"We believe AI should expand educational opportunity, which is why we designed ChatGPT for Teens to support moments outside the classroom when help is not always available, while keeping teens engaged in an active and collaborative learning process."

— OpenAI, company blog post

The company said it is using AI to estimate users' ages and will apply these protections to anyone suspected of being under 18, regardless of what birthdate appears in their profile. In the European Union, the feature will roll out in the coming weeks due to regulatory requirements.

A Response to Mounting Lawsuits

The launch comes as the $852 billion startup faces a string of lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT contributed to real-world harm to young people. In April, seven families of victims of a school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the shooter had extensive chatbot conversations related to gun violence. Altman apologized to the families.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8s0EV45rLu8

In June, the state of Florida sued OpenAI, accusing it of helping mass shooters, encouraging suicide, and getting minors addicted to a tool with "no parental oversight." Just last week, a Massachusetts district attorney charged a 17-year-old with two counts of murder, noting the teen had been engaged in ChatGPT conversations about "theoretical ideas or fantasies regarding killing his family."

Lauren Jonas, OpenAI's head of youth and families, told CNN that "any one of these instances is too many."

"Our safety work is never done. This is 24/7, 365, a continuous effort to make sure that we're getting teens the support they need in the moments they need it."

— Lauren Jonas, OpenAI's Head of Youth and Families

Tools for Parents

Enhanced controls allow parents to link their accounts with their teen's, adjust settings through a simple control panel, and receive notifications in high-risk situations. OpenAI said it will add alerts related to eating disorders in the coming weeks.

Teens can unlink their accounts at any time, but parents will be notified if they do. OpenAI acknowledged that guardrails are "not foolproof and can be bypassed" and encouraged parents to maintain ongoing conversations about healthy AI use.

For users mistakenly placed in the under-18 experience, a verification process through Persona, a secure third-party identity service, allows them to restore full access via a selfie upload.

The Bigger Picture

Nearly a third of American teens use AI chatbots daily, according to a Pew Research Center study published in December 2025. ChatGPT was by far the most popular, with more than half of teen chatbot users reporting they had used it.

Common Sense Media's Robbie Torney called the parental controls "a good starting point" but emphasized they work best "when combined with ongoing conversations about responsible AI use, clear family rules about technology, and active involvement in understanding what their teen is doing online."

As OpenAI prepares for a potentially record-breaking initial public offering, the teen safety push signals the company's effort to get ahead of regulators and critics who argue that AI companies have moved too slowly to protect their youngest users.
